work_packages.title: Thompson Sampling Backend for Parameter Tuning
work_packages.description: Implement single Thompson Sampling (D6) as the sole parameter tuning mechanism, replacing Optuna. Maintains posterior distributions (Beta distributions for bounded parameters, Normal distributions for continuous parameters) over parameter effectiveness. Each tunable parameter has an associated posterior that is updated based on observed rewards (execution quality metrics). Sampling from posteriors balances exploration (trying less-tested parameter values) vs exploitation (using values known to perform well). This is a lightweight, dependency-free implementation using only numpy/scipy for distribution sampling and update.
acceptance_criteria: ThompsonSampler class supports registering tunable parameters with type (bounded_discrete, bounded_continuous), prior distribution config, and hard bounds
sample() method returns one sampled value per registered parameter from its current posterior distribution
update(parameter_name, reward: float) method updates the posterior distribution for a single parameter using Bayesian update rules (Beta-Bernoulli for discrete bins, Normal-Normal for continuous)
Posterior distributions are serializable to/from JSON for checkpoint persistence
Convergence test: after 200+ reward observations favoring a specific parameter region, sampled values concentrate (>80%) within ±10% of the optimal region
No dependency on Optuna, hyperopt, or any external optimization framework
deliverables: thompson_sampler.py — ThompsonSampler class with register/sample/update/persist methods
tests/test_thompson_sampler.py — Unit tests including convergence validation

work_packages.title: LLM-as-Optimizer Interface for Parameter Suggestion
work_packages.description: Implement LLMOptimizer (D5) replacing traditional optimization frameworks. Uses structured prompt to analyze execution metrics (Quality Gate pass rates, token consumption per task, loop iteration counts, failure/retry counts) and suggest parameter adjustments. The LLM receives a snapshot of recent execution performance + current parameter values + Thompson Sampling posteriors summary, then outputs structured JSON with suggested adjustments. This is a suggestion layer — all suggestions pass through ParameterSafetyGuard before application. The prompt enforces Role+Context+Constraints+Output schema pattern per AI Native principles (4.1).
acceptance_criteria: LLMOptimizer class accepts execution_metrics dict (quality_gate_pass_rate, avg_token_consumption, avg_loop_iterations, failure_count, retry_count) and current_params dict

build_prompt() method generates a structured prompt with: role (parameter optimization expert), context (current metrics + parameter state), constraints (safety bounds reference), output schema (JSON with parameter_name, suggested_value, reasoning, confidence)
parse_response() method validates LLM output against expected JSON schema using Pydantic, rejects malformed responses
suggest() method returns List[ParameterSuggestion] where each suggestion includes parameter_name, suggested_value, reasoning, confidence_score (0-1)
Handles LLM failures gracefully: timeout, malformed JSON, or out-of-bounds suggestions return empty list with logged warning (no crash)
Prompt template is stored as a separate constant, not hardcoded in logic flow
deliverables: llm_optimizer.py — LLMOptimizer class with build_prompt/parse_response/suggest methods + prompt template
models.py — ParameterSuggestion Pydantic model for structured output
tests/test_llm_optimizer.py — Unit tests with mocked LLM responses (valid, malformed, out-of-bounds)

work_packages.title: Parameter Safety Guard (Bounds + Cooling + Amplitude)
work_packages.description: Implement ParameterSafetyGuard enforcing R9 constraints: hard upper/lower bounds on all tunable parameters, cooling period between adjustments to prevent oscillation, and ±50% amplitude limits per adjustment cycle. This is the last line of defense — no parameter change bypasses this guard. Hard bounds are absolute (clamp or reject). Cooling period is a configurable minimum time interval (default: 5 minutes) between consecutive adjustments to the same parameter. Amplitude limit caps any single adjustment to ±50% of the parameter's current value (prevents drastic jumps). All guard actions are logged with reason for audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: ParameterSafetyGuard class initialized with parameter_specs dict: {param_name: {lower_bound, upper_bound, cooling_period_seconds, current_value}}

validate(suggestions: List[ParameterSuggestion]) returns List[ValidatedAdjustment] where each adjustment is guaranteed within hard bounds (clamped), within amplitude limits (clamped to ±50% of current value), and respects cooling period (rejected if too soon)
Cooling period tracked per-parameter with monotonic timestamps; adjustment to a parameter rejected if last adjustment was < cooling_period_seconds ago
Amplitude limit: |suggested_value - current_value| / current_value <= 0.5; values exceeding this are clamped to the boundary
All rejections and clamps logged with structured reason (which constraint triggered, original vs adjusted value)
apply(adjustments) atomically updates current values and cooling timestamps after validation passes
Unit test: suggestion of value 10x current → clamped to 1.5x current (±50% limit)
Unit test: suggestion within cooling period → rejected with reason
Unit test: suggestion outside hard bounds → clamped to bound
deliverables: safety_guard.py — ParameterSafetyGuard class with validate/apply methods + constraint checking logic
tests/test_safety_guard.py — Unit tests for hard bounds, cooling period, amplitude limits, and combined scenarios

work_packages.title: MetaLoopEngine — Integration + Metrics Collector
work_packages.description: Implement MetaLoopEngine as the orchestrating class that ties together Thompson Sampling, LLM-as-Optimizer, and ParameterSafetyGuard into a closed feedback loop. Also implements the execution metrics collector that feeds the loop. The engine exposes: (1) record_metrics(execution_id, metrics_dict) to ingest execution data, (2) optimize_cycle() to run one full optimization cycle (collect metrics → LLM suggests → safety guard validates → Thompson Sampling updates posteriors → apply safe adjustments), (3) get_current_params() for other components to read tuned parameters. The metrics collector aggregates raw execution data into summary statistics (rolling window of last N executions) that feed the LLM optimizer prompt.
acceptance_criteria: MetaLoopEngine class initialized with config: parameter_specs, llm_client, optimization_interval_seconds, metrics_window_size (default: 50 executions)

record_metrics(execution_id, metrics) stores metrics in a bounded rolling window (deque with maxlen); metrics include quality_gate_pass_rate, token_consumption, loop_iterations, failure_count, retry_count, timestamp

optimize_cycle() executes the full loop: aggregate metrics → call LLMOptimizer.suggest() → call ParameterSafetyGuard.validate() → call ThompsonSampler.update() with reward signal derived from metrics → call ParameterSafetyGuard.apply() → log audit entry
get_current_params() returns dict of current tuned parameter values, thread-safe
Metrics aggregation produces summary dict with rolling averages, min/max, trend direction for each metric
Full cycle audit trail: each optimize_cycle() generates audit entry with timestamp, metrics_summary, suggestions_received, suggestions_applied, suggestions_rejected, rejection_reasons
Integration test: 10-cycle optimization with simulated metrics showing convergence
Integration test: safety guard rejects out-of-bounds suggestions, verified no parameter exceeds hard bounds
deliverables: metrics_collector.py — MetricsCollector with rolling window aggregation
audit.py — Audit logger for optimization cycles
tests/test_meta_loop_engine.py — Integration tests for full optimization loop
tests/test_metrics_collector.py — Unit tests for metrics aggregation

optional_suggestions: Consider adding a 'dry_run' mode to optimize_cycle() that logs what would change without applying, useful for debugging and validation
Thompson Sampling posterior distributions could be visualized via metrics exporter (Observability worker) for monitoring convergence
LLM-as-Optimizer prompt could include few-shot examples of good vs bad parameter suggestions to improve suggestion quality
